_provenance.what: The 20 ambiguous interaction restraints (AIRs) that the 2017 ClusPro protocol uses for its own worked E2A-HPr example. NOT the 20 NOE distances themselves: the NOE measurements are Wang et al., EMBO J 19:5635-5649 (2000), which this repository does not hold, and the AIRs derived from them are Dominguez, Boelens & Bonvin, JACS 125:1731-1737 (2003) [ja026939x] supplementary file S2.
_provenance.cited_by: Kozakov, Hall, Xia, Porter, Padhorny, Yueh, Beglov & Vajda, 'The ClusPro web server for protein-protein docking', Nature Protocols 12(2):255-278 (2017), published p.273 = PMC author manuscript p.21, 'Accounting for pairwise distance restraint'.
_provenance.checked: Both files parsed independently and required to agree: 20 groups; 11 anchored on E2A and 9 on HPr; every receptor and ligand residue list identical group for group; one distance convention across the set; every ClusPro group carrying required=1; ClusPro restraint type 'residue'. The script refuses to write on any mismatch.

receptor.molecule: glucose-specific phosphocarrier protein IIAglc (E2A), unbound X-ray

ligand.molecule: histidine-containing phosphocarrier protein HPr, unbound X-ray

adopted.meaning: minimum heavy-atom separation between the two residues

air_original.meaning: HADDOCK effective distance, <d^-6>^(-1/6) over all atom pairs

distance_convention.note: The two are different quantities, not two roundings of one. JuPIPER's Restraint is a minimum-separation test, so the ClusPro reading is the one it can express; the AIR numbers are recorded so the substitution is visible.

group_cutoff.meaning: RestraintGroup cutoff, i.e. MORE THAN 0 members satisfied = at least one. This is the AIR semantics and matches every published group's required=1.

set_cutoff.meaning: How many of the 20 groups a translation must satisfy. The protocol (p.8) says 'the required number of restraint groups', and the published JSON carries no set-level field. Swept by scripts/validate_constraints.jl rather than guessed.

_provenance.status: [MEASURED] as a transcription of two fetched, mutually cross-checked files. The distance reading is [ASSUMED] (see distance_convention) and the set-level cutoff is [UNPUBLISHED].
